plan.title: bug: deft update on current npm deposit creates phantom dirty tree on Windows and over-reports changes

narratives.Description: bug: deft update on current npm deposit creates phantom dirty tree on Windows and over-reports changes
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Running `deft update` on a consumer project that is **already on the latest npm release** (`@deftai/directive@0.65.0`) produces a misleading operator/agent experience on Windows:

1. ~280 files under `.deft/core/` appear modified in `git status` even though content is unchanged.
2. The installer prints a long list of paths as "uncommitted changes" and implies a framework deposit commit is needed.
3. The only real diff (ignoring line endings) is a `fetched_at` timestamp bump in `.deft/core/VERSION`.

This caused a maintainer to investigate whether a commit was required after syncing master and running the canonical npm upgrade path — it was not.

## Environment

- **Consumer repo:** `deftai/statusreport` (master at `6173aad`, already on directive v0.65.0 via PR #83)
- **OS:** Windows 10, PowerShell
- **Git:** `core.autocrlf=true`
- **Node:** v22.14.0
- **Global CLI:** `@deftai/directive@0.65.0` (installed via `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`)
- **Deposit:** `.deft/core/VERSION` shows `managed_by: npm`, `ref: v0.65.0`

## Repro

```powershell
git checkout master
git pull origin master   # already at v0.65.0
npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest
deft update
git status --short       # ~280 modified files under .deft/core/
git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat   # only .deft/core/VERSION (fetched_at line)
```

## Expected

When `previous_version === content_version` and payload content is unchanged:

- Clear message: **already current — no repository commit required**
- Do **not** list every touched path as uncommitted framework deposit changes
- Working tree should remain clean (or guidance should explain line-ending-only phantom diffs immediately)

## Actual

`deft update` output (abridged):

```
✓ Deft framework payload refreshed.
  Content      : v0.65.0
  previous_version: 0.65.0
```

Plus a long "AGENTS.md refresh side effects" / uncommitted-changes list (~280 paths).

`git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` shows **one** real change:

```diff
--- a/.deft/core/VERSION
+++ b/.deft/core/VERSION
-fetched_at: '2026-06-30T14:53:46Z'
+fetched_at: '2026-06-30T15:57:01Z'
```

All other "modified" files are CRLF/LF phantom diffs from `core.autocrlf=true` interacting with LF npm deposit writes.

## Root causes (proposed)

1. **Missing `eol=lf` projection for `.deft/core/**`**
   - Consumer `.gitattributes` has `linguist-generated` / `linguist-vendored` but not `text eol=lf`.
   - `deft update` reports ".gitattributes already marks .deft/core/** … — skipping" and does not add the LF pin.
   - Same pattern already exists in statusreport for `frontend/src/generated/*.ts text eol=lf` to stabilize CI diffs across autocrlf settings.

2. **No no-op refresh detection**
   - File-swap runs even when tarball content matches on-disk deposit.
   - `fetched_at` is rewritten anyway, creating a tempting-but-meaningless commit.

3. **Over-aggressive post-update reporting**
   - Installer lists all touched paths as deposit-side uncommitted changes without distinguishing semantic diffs from line-ending noise.

## Proposed fixes

### P1 — `.gitattributes` projection

Extend consumer `.gitattributes` projection to add (when missing):

```gitattributes
.deft/core/** text eol=lf
```

Idempotent; mirrors frontend codegen stability pattern.

### P1 — No-op update path

When content hash / version unchanged:

- Skip file-swap (or skip reporting touched paths)
- Print explicit "already current" exit summary
- Do not rewrite `VERSION.fetched_at` unless content actually changed

### P2 — Windows post-update hint

If deposit version unchanged and git working tree dirty, suggest:

```powershell
git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat
git checkout -- .deft/core/   # when only CRLF phantom diffs
```

### P2 — Sync / UPGRADING guidance

Document that re-running `deft update` on current master often produces **no commit-worthy changes**; version bump commits happen only when `ref`/`tag` in `VERSION` changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Repro above on Windows + `core.autocrlf=true` leaves clean `git status` after `deft update` when already on latest release
- [ ] `deft update` on unchanged deposit prints "already current" (no false deposit-commit nudge)
- [ ] Fresh `deft update` on a project without eol pin adds `.deft/core/** text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes`
- [ ] `VERSION.fetched_at` not bumped on idempotent refresh
- [ ] Test or fixture covering no-op update path (consumer install smoke)

## Related

- #2120 — Windows native `engine:_ts-build` doubles `DEFT_ROOT`; `task deft:verify:cache-fresh` fails (separate bug, same session, first native-Windows run vs WSL)

## Labels rationale

Bug: incorrect/misleading behavior after canonical upgrade path. Also affects agent-experience and adoption (operators/agents infer a commit is needed when it is not).
